Description: An abstract class representing any entity, which is a physical, digital, conceptual, or other kind of thing with some fixed aspects; entities may be real or imaginary
A class representing devices that are used to carry out an activity: instruments, sensors, containers, also any human-operated devices used in manual observations
For types of devices used specifically in field sampling activities
For types of devices used specifically to make observations and measurements (in the field or in the lab)
A class representing permits, which describe the authorisation to carry out an activity, often needing to be approved by a legal/regulatory entity
A class representing platforms, which are entities on/from which a device is deployed (e.g. a ship, a buoy, a CTD carousel, an ROV, etc.)

A class representing protocols, which describe how an activity was done, including the design, methodology, method steps, materials, statistical considerations, etc. Sometimes also called Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
A class representing samples, which consist of biological or environmental material, or any extracts of that material

A class representing software, being software applications or computer programming source code, but can also be computational workflows, notebooks, and even simple processes such as basic arithmetical calculations
An abstract class representing the agent responsible for an activity. This can be a Person or Organization
A class to represent agents which are social or legal organisations such as a company, project, society, etc
A class to represent agents which are people
The place at which an activity occurs.
An abstract class representing any activity, which is something that occurs over a period of time, is performed by an agent, and acts upon or with objects/entities
An abstract class representing any activity that deals with physical material
A class representing activities where physical material is acquired from an agent (e.g. ordered from a biobank)
A class representing activities where the physical material is moved, posted, shipped
A class representing physical activities where the work done on the physical material transforms that material, e.g. adding preservatives, filtering, centrifuging, extracting, etc
A class representing physical activities where measurements are made from or of physical material (such as water, organisms, media, laboratory, etc)
A class representing acquiring activities where material is collected from the field
A class representing physical activities where material is retained in a specific location (e.g. storage facility, freezer, etc.), for some length of time

A class representing storing activities where the physical material is stored in a long-term storage facility (such as a biobank or culture collection facility) specifically to make it available for others to use
An abstract class representing any activity that has a digital nature
A class representing digital activities where the digital objects are obtained from another digital source, e.g. an online catalogue, a colleague’s spreadsheet
A class representing digital activities where the digital objects are processed;  ‘processing’ can range from simple calculations to complete workflows
Only for the RDF implementation
Only for the RDF implementation
